title: Dataverse security roles: who can read or change which data?
summary: The documented permission model, licensing qualifications, commands and audit controls are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The application-user creation path needs a minor clarification of the application-selection steps it skips.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Dataverse security roles group privileges governing access to tables and records within an environment.
claims.quote: Use security roles to configure access to all resources in an environment or to specific apps and data in the environment.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: The Dataverse security model applies only to environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: The model applies only to environments that have a Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Table privileges include Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append to, Assign and Share.
claims.quote: Table privileges define which tasks a user with access to a table record can do, such as Read, Create, Delete, Write, Assign, Share, Append, and Append To.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Security roles include miscellaneous task privileges.
claims.quote: Miscellaneous privileges: These task-based privileges give a user permission to perform specific, miscellaneous (nonrecord) tasks, such as publish articles or activate business rules.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Security roles include privacy-related privileges such as exporting to Excel.
claims.quote: Privacy-related privileges: These privileges give a user permission to perform tasks that involve data that's integrated, downloaded, or exported outside of Dataverse, such as exporting data to Microsoft Excel or printing.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: A privilege's access level determines its reach through the business unit hierarchy.
claims.quote: Access levels determine how deep in the business unit hierarchy the user can perform the privilege.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: The access levels are Organization, Parent: Child Business Unit, Business Unit, User and None.
claims.quote: Organization ... Parent: Child Business Unit ... Business Unit ... User ... None

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges have only Organization or None access levels.
claims.quote: For organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges only have access levels of Organization or None.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Security roles can be assigned directly to users.
claims.quote: Assign security roles directly to users or to Dataverse teams.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Security roles can be assigned to Dataverse teams.
claims.quote: Assign security roles directly to users or to Dataverse teams.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Team members receive the privileges assigned to their team.
claims.quote: Team members receive the privileges assigned to the team.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: A user can hold multiple security roles.
claims.quote: A user can have multiple security roles.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Cumulative access
claims.claim: Role and team privileges accumulate, so a narrower role cannot remove access granted by a broader role.
claims.quote: Security privileges are cumulative. A user receives the broadest access granted by all their roles and team memberships.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Business units define security boundaries.
claims.quote: They define security boundaries that help you manage users and data.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person; Governance controls
claims.claim: Security roles are associated with business units.
claims.quote: Security roles are associated with business units.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Every user belongs to a business unit.
claims.quote: Every user in an environment belongs to a business unit.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Tenant-level administrator roles are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant-level admin roles such as Power Platform administrator and Dynamics 365 administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: A tenant administrator role does not itself grant Dataverse data access; System Administrator is needed in the particular environment.
claims.quote: To work with data in a Dataverse environment, a tenant admin must also be assigned the System Administrator Dataverse security role in that specific environment.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Environments without Dataverse have only Environment Admin and Environment Maker as their predefined environment roles.
claims.quote: Environment Maker and Environment Admin are the only predefined roles for environments that have no Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Column-level security is configured separately from record-level role access.
claims.quote: Enable column-level security separately for each column. Then create a column security profile that grants Create, Update, and Read access to secured columns.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership is preview
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership is in preview.
claims.quote: Filtered table record ownership (preview)

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership grants record access through column-value filters.
claims.quote: Filtered record ownership lets admins control access to Dataverse records with column-value filters.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Basic User is automatically assigned to every user added in Dataverse in the Default environment type.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Environment Maker is automatically assigned to every user added in Dataverse in the Default environment type.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Environment Maker for Copilot Studio authors.
claims.quote: Assign the Environment Maker role to users who need to author agents.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Another predefined or custom role can provide Copilot Studio authoring permissions.
claims.quote: If the user needs a different set of permissions, assign another predefined role or a custom role.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Tenant administrators no longer automatically receive the Dataverse System Administrator role.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: Removing a tenant administrator role does not automatically remove an existing Dataverse System Administrator assignment.
claims.quote: removing them from the Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 service admin roles will not automatically remove their System Administrator role in Dataverse.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft's security role pages document no separate price, licence or meter specific to security roles themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse security roles separate price license meter security role pricing. Read security-roles-privileges, database-security, assign-security-roles, wp-security-cds and pricing-billing-skus; no separate role price, licence or meter found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A user's presence in an environment does not grant Dataverse data access.
claims.quote: A user's presence in an environment doesn't grant access to Dataverse data.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits: Everyone needs a role
claims.claim: Users need at least one security role, directly or through a group team, or the service denies access.
claims.quote: You must assign at least one security role to every user either directly or indirectly as a member of a group team. The service doesn't allow access to users who don't have at least one security role.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users still need any required product licence in addition to an appropriate role.
claims.quote: The user must still have an appropriate security role and any required product license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database.
claims.quote: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse data access requires an appropriate Dataverse licence.
claims.quote: the user must have an appropriate Dataverse license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Where licence-to-role mappings exist, users with valid licences receive the mapped roles automatically.
claims.quote: Users, with a valid license, get corresponding mapped roles assigned to them automatically.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Removing a licence automatically removes its corresponding mapped role.
claims.quote: Removal of the respective license results in automatic role removal.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Licence-based default role management does not apply to Dataverse for Teams, Trial or Developer environments.
claims.quote: License-based default role management isn't applicable for users in these types of environments: Dataverse for Teams, Trial, and Developer.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: An application user can be created without a licence.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Elevation guard
claims.claim: A person assigning security roles cannot assign a role with more privileges than they hold.
claims.quote: the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Elevation guard
claims.claim: Delegating role assignment to non-System Administrators calls for a custom security role.
claims.quote: If you have a need to allow non-System Administrators to assign security roles, you should consider creating a custom security role

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The predefined-role reference says its listed predefined roles cannot be edited.
claims.quote: The following list provides the predefined security roles in an environment that has a Dataverse database. You can't edit these roles.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The editing guide documents editing role privileges but excludes System Administrator.
claims.quote: You can't edit the System Administrator security role. Instead, copy the System Administrator security role and make changes to the new role.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Where copying is supported, a security role can be copied and the copy's privileges changed.
claims.quote:
Go back to the Security roles page and select the new role you created.
13. Specify privileges for the security role.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Some predefined roles cannot be copied; Microsoft suggests creating a custom role instead.
claims.quote: Some predefined roles can't be copied. Try creating a custom security role instead.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.
claims.quote: It's important to note that custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Organization-level access; What to check
claims.claim: Organization-level access reaches records across all business units.
claims.quote: Users can access all records in the organization, regardless of the business unit hierarchical level they or the environment belong to.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Sharing is the exception
claims.claim: Microsoft advises record sharing for exceptions because it is less efficient and harder to troubleshoot.
claims.quote: Use sharing only for exceptions because it performs less efficiently and can be harder to troubleshoot than role-based access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Roles do not unlock columns
claims.claim: A column security profile can grant secured-column access only after the user has record access.
claims.quote: Column-level security doesn't grant access to a record. A user must already have record access before a column security profile can grant access to secured columns.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Dataverse solutions move security roles between environments.
claims.quote: Use Dataverse solutions to move security roles and column security profiles between environments.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Business units must be managed separately in each environment.
claims.quote: Create and manage business units and teams separately in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Teams must be managed separately in each environment.
claims.quote: Create and manage business units and teams separately in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Users must be assigned to security components separately in each environment.
claims.quote: You must also assign users to the appropriate security components in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership is preview
claims.claim: Microsoft says preview features are not meant for production use.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.where: Risks and limits: PowerShell gap; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment applies to environments without Dataverse and returns 403 Forbidden when a Dataverse database exists.
claims.quote: Sets permissions to an environment without a Dataverse database. If you make this call to an environment with a Dataverse database instance, you receive a 403 Forbidden error.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Assigning Dataverse roles requires System Administrator or a custom role with at least Read and Assign on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: Assign Dataverse security roles | System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and Global Administrators must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role. They must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group.
claims.quote: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group. This restriction doesn't apply to Global Administrators or Power Platform Administrators.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Business units restrict available role assignments unless record ownership across business units is enabled.
claims.quote: When the allow record ownership across business units is enabled, you can assign security roles from different business units to your users irrespective of which business unit the users belong to.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 53 records assigning a security role to a team.
claims.quote: 53 | Assign Role To Team | Associate | A security role is assigned to a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 54 records removing a security role from a team.
claims.quote: 54 | Remove Role From Team | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 55 records assigning a security role to a user.
claims.quote: 55 | Assign Role To User | Associate | A security role is assigned to a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 56 records removing a security role from a user.
claims.quote: 56 | Remove Role From User | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Data policies let administrators control connector access.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.

claims.claim: Direct user role assignments are managed through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.

Select Users + permissions, and then select Users.

claims.claim: POST to the v9.0 systemuserroles_association/$ref endpoint assigns a role, identified by @odata.id, to a user identified by their Entra object ID.

claims.where: controls[2].ui
claims.claim: The application-user creation path runs through Application users > + New app user > Create a new app user > edit icon for security roles.
claims.quote: Select + Add an app to choose the registered Microsoft Entra application that was created for the selected user, and then select Add.
claims.fix: Use the fuller path 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > Create a new app user > + Add an app > application > Add > Business Unit > business unit > edit icon (security roles)'. Keep the note explaining the application and business-unit selections; these omitted target selections are not a blocker.

claims.where: controls[2].api
claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment-id> --user <application-id> --role <role> --application-user assigns an application user its security role.
claims.quote:
pac admin assign-user `
  --environment 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 `
  --user 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 `
  --role "System Administrator"
  --application-user

claims.where: controls[2].note
claims.claim: An environment permits only one application user per Microsoft Entra app registration.
